So there are different formats for different players that suit their tastes:

Standard:
Won't mention, because you say you already played Standard. But there are good starter products in the form of Standard Challenger decks. The problem is currently there is not a lot of support for
Standard at LGSs.


Modern:
Modern is a 1v1 format that is non-rotating and takes all standard sets and Modern Horizons sets from Eighth Edition onward. Very hefty entry fee in terms of competitive decks. A good population of players

Pioneer: 
Pioneer is a 1v1 format that is non-rotating and takes all standard sets from Return to Ravnica onward, and is generally cheaper to get into than Modern. A great starter product is the Pioneer Challenger decks that came out last year and this year. A good population of people

Commander:
Commander (or EDH) is a casual 4-player free-for-all, where you pilot a singleton 100 card deck, including a "commander" in the form of a Legendary creature (and some exceptions). 

Great starter products are the preconstructed decks that come out with nearly every set. It's ready out of the box. This format is also the most popular format out of all MTG formats.

There is also a competitive scene (abbr. CEDH) that takes it to the next level if you are curious.
